claim: The alpha~4 holographic force law (stress-tensor exchange) measured via chi=3 MERA on Quantinuum Helios can be reproduced on a Rydberg tweezer array (QuEra Aquila or Pasqal Vela) using a blockade-constrained MERA, yielding a force exponent within 10% of alpha=4.0 despite the modified PXP Hamiltonian geometry.
confidence_rationale: PAPER-2026-061 (Sahay/Lin/Cotler PRX 2025) explicitly demonstrates that the Rydberg PXP Hamiltonian realizes an Ising CFT and that holographic circuits are implementable on current tweezer arrays. Our existing alpha~4 result has three independent measurements converging (SIM-2026-015, SIM-2026-015d, SIM-2026-016). Medium confidence (not high) because the blockade-modified MERA introduces new parameters not present in our existing chi=3 MERA, and the mapping from our transverse-field Ising chain MERA to the PXP Hamiltonian requires non-trivial circuit adaptation. Multiple independent source chains (Sahay PRX + our SIM results) converge, making this stronger than low.
test_design: 1. Map our existing chi=3 16-qubit MERA circuit (from SIM-2026-015 ansatz) to a blockade-constrained PXP MERA following Sahay/Lin/Cotler (PAPER-2026-061) prescription. Identify which two-qubit gates require blockade-compatible decompositions. 2. Compile target circuit for QuEra Aquila native gate set (CZ gates via Rydberg blockade). Estimate two-qubit gate depth and required coherence time. 3. Request cloud access via AWS Braket (QuEra Aquila, 256 atoms). Run chi=3 blockade-MERA at N=8 and N=16 qubit chains embedded in tweezer array. Collect ~5000 shots per measurement setting. 4. Compute conditional mutual information C(r) across chain separations dr=1..6. Fit power-law alpha via scipy curve_fit with error propagation. 5. Compare measured alpha to our prior alpha=3.92+/-0.16 (24q exact, SIM-2026-011) and alpha=4.07+/-0.18 (16q chi=3 MERA, SIM-2026-015d). Test H0: alpha_Rydberg = alpha_Helios within combined 1-sigma error bars.
refutation_criteria: If the measured power-law exponent alpha_Rydberg differs from 4.0 by more than 15% (i.e., alpha < 3.4 or alpha > 4.6) at 3-sigma significance with N=16 Rydberg circuit, the blockade-MERA does not replicate our holographic force law and the PXP Hamiltonian geometry introduces a qualitatively different bulk geometry. Alternatively, if the CMI signal is indistinguishable from random noise (SNR < 2 at all dr values), the blockade-modified MERA fails to maintain sufficient entanglement structure for holographic force detection.
hardware_required: QuEra Aquila (256 neutral-atom tweezer, cloud via AWS Braket) or Pasqal Vela (European cloud). Local CPU for circuit compilation and classical simulation baseline. No cryogenics required. Estimated cloud cost: ~$500-2000 for 50,000 total shots across N=8 and N=16 runs.

feasibility_notes.hardware: QuEra Aquila (256 neutral atoms, cloud via AWS Braket) is operational now. CZ gate fidelity ~99.5%, coherence time sufficient for 16-qubit PXP-MERA depth. Pasqal Vela is an alternative. Both available without institutional access.
feasibility_notes.circuit: 16-qubit chi=3 blockade-MERA requires ~40-80 two-qubit CZ gates. At 99.5% per gate, cumulative fidelity ~67-82%. Our SIM-2026-015c showed chi=3 MERA force signal survives at 0.15% error rate at 16q, suggesting this fidelity regime is sufficient for force detection at dr=1..4. Gate depth is within QuEra Aquila's demonstrated coherent operation window.
feasibility_notes.math: PAPER-2026-061 analytically proves the PXP Hamiltonian gives Ising CFT and the holographic circuit is implementable on tweezer arrays. No no-go theorems apply. Blockade constraint introduces corrections to standard MERA unitaries but does not prevent implementation.
feasibility_notes.resource: AWS Braket QuEra Aquila pricing: ~$0.01/task + $0.0009/shot. 50,000 shots ~ $500 total. Well within $10k-$50k budget. Classical post-processing: NumPy CMI computation, local CPU.

pipeline_provenance.conjecture_stage: Generated from PAPER-2026-061 (Rydberg PXP = Ising CFT, blockade MERA realizable on current tweezer arrays) cross-referenced with our confirmed alpha~4 result (SIM-2026-015, SIM-2026-016). This is the most strategic hypothesis because it extends our holographic force result to a fundamentally different physical platform (neutral atom tweezers vs trapped-ion Helios), testing whether the alpha~4 exponent is platform-independent as expected for a CFT universal quantity. The key scientific question is whether the blockade constraint introduces corrections to the MERA entanglement structure that shift the effective force exponent. PAPER-2026-062 provides additional motivation: hyperbolic lattice Rydberg arrays naturally encode AdS/CFT boundary correspondence.
